fix: apply UI additional http headers only for requests to UI assets (#3853)

The additional UI http headers are added to each api requests. They add
extra bytes to each api call without any value (up to 15-20% of request
size). This work rearrange the code to apply those headers only for
requests to UI assets.

fix(ui): ui.topbar.color config setting has been broken since v1.53.0 (#3857)

The regression when `/meta/config` was replaced with `/meta/info` for
UI.

feat: rewrite v1 install script with robust version detection

Complete rewrite of the main branch install script to match the v2 version
but adapted for v1-only releases:

**Major improvements:**
- Robust v1-only version detection using /releases endpoint with JSON parsing
- Filters out prereleases, drafts, and v2 releases entirely
- Structured logging with color-coded info/warn/error messages
- Modular platform detection functions (OS and architecture)
- Enhanced error handling and user feedback
- Flexible installation directory support via BIN_DIR environment variable
- POSIX-compliant (no 'local' keywords, passes shellcheck)

**v1-specific behavior:**
- Only accepts and installs v1.x.x releases
- Explicitly rejects v2.x.x versions with clear error message
- Finds latest stable v1 release even if newer v2 releases exist
- Uses same robust JSON parsing as v2 script but filters for v1

**Future-proof design:**
- Will continue to install latest stable v1 release regardless of v2 releases
- Properly excludes beta/alpha/rc versions by checking GitHub's prerelease flag
- Resilient to GitHub API changes with comprehensive error handling

**Testing verified:**
- ✅ Installs latest v1.59.2 release correctly
- ✅ Rejects v2.0.0 with clear error message
- ✅ Installs specific v1 versions (e.g., v1.59.0)
- ✅ Passes shellcheck with no warnings
- ✅ Cross-platform compatibility

This provides v1 users with the same robust, user-friendly installation
experience as the v2 script while maintaining strict v1-only behavior.

feat(metrics): add Git sync observability metrics to feature flag backend (#4673)

* This change enhances Flipt's Git-based feature flag backend observability by adding detailed synchronization metrics. Currently, failures during Git sync are only logged without metric visibility, limiting proactive monitoring and alerting capabilities.

    - Introduce new OpenTelemetry metrics for Git sync operations:
      - Last sync time as an observable gauge (timestamp).
      - Sync duration histogram.
      - Counters for number of flags fetched.
      - Success and failure counts with failure reason attributes.

    - Instrument the `SnapshotStore.update` method, the core sync loop, to record these metrics accurately on every sync attempt, including partial failures and cleanups.

    - Extend the `Snapshot` type with `TotalFlagsCount()` to count all flags across namespaces for metric reporting.

    - Integrate metrics initialization in app startup ensuring consistent telemetry setup.

    - Improve test coverage by suggesting strategies to verify metric emission and sync behavior.

    These metric additions enable operators to monitor Git sync health, detect failures promptly, and troubleshoot issues efficiently, significantly improving runtime observability and system reliability.

fix(license): resolve timeout issues during license deactivation on shutdown (#4486)

* fix(license): resolve timeout issues during license deactivation on shutdown

The license manager was experiencing timeout errors during shutdown when
attempting to deactivate licenses with the Keygen API. This occurred due
to two issues:

1. No explicit timeout on the HTTP client, causing requests to hang
   indefinitely when the Keygen API was slow or unreachable
2. License deactivation competing with other shutdown operations for
   the shared 30-second shutdown context

Changes:
- Add 10-second timeout to retryable HTTP client for Keygen API calls
- Reduce retry attempts from 5 to 3 for faster failure detection
- Use dedicated 15-second timeout context for license deactivation
- Prevent deactivation from being cancelled by other shutdown operations

This ensures license deactivation completes within a reasonable timeframe
while maintaining graceful shutdown behavior and allowing licenses to be

feat: optimize CI integration tests with registry cache (#4516)

* feat: add registry cache optimization for CI integration tests

Implement Docker BuildKit registry cache sharing across GitHub Actions jobs to reduce CI build times.

- Add BuildWithCache() and TestWithCache() Dagger functions
- Add build-cache job that builds once and pushes to GHCR
- Modify integration test jobs to reuse cached images
- Generate cache keys from git commit and source file hashes
- Expected ~60% reduction in total pipeline time

Signed-off-by: Mark Phelps <209477+markphelps@users.noreply.github.com>

* fix: correct Dagger command syntax for cached integration tests

The --cases flag should be passed to the integration subcommand, not the test-with-cache command.

Fixed command structure:
test-with-cache --source . --cached-image <image> integration --cases <cases>

Signed-off-by: Mark Phelps <209477+markphelps@users.noreply.github.com>

* fix: ensure cached image reference is always populated

The cache image output was empty when cache hit occurred because we were only setting
the image reference conditionally. Now we always set the expected image reference
regardless of cache hit/miss status.

Signed-off-by: Mark Phelps <209477+markphelps@users.noreply.github.com>

* fix: remove unused IMAGE_REF variable

Clean up the shell script by directly using the env vars instead of an intermediate variable.

Signed-off-by: Mark Phelps <209477+markphelps@users.noreply.github.com>

* docs: add registry cache optimization details to build/CLAUDE.md

Document the new caching approach including:
- Registry cache strategy and workflow
- Performance benefits and expected improvements
- Cache management and troubleshooting
- New Dagger cache-related functions
- Debug commands for cache issues

Signed-off-by: Mark Phelps <209477+markphelps@users.noreply.github.com>

* fix: use lightweight base container when using cached images

The TestWithCache function was still rebuilding the full base container from scratch,
defeating the purpose of the cache optimization. Now when using cached images:

- Use lightweight test runner (golang:1.24-alpine3.21 + basic tools)
- Skip expensive Go build environment setup
- Only mount source code needed for test execution

This should significantly improve the cache performance in CI.

Signed-off-by: Mark Phelps <209477+markphelps@users.noreply.github.com>

* chore: rm --race for ITs

Signed-off-by: Mark Phelps <209477+markphelps@users.noreply.github.com>

* feat: optimize container builds with multi-layered registry caching

Implement comprehensive build optimization using registry-backed caching
for all build stages to dramatically reduce CI build times.

- golang-base: Cached Go toolchain with build dependencies
- golang-deps: Cached Go module dependencies
- node-base: Cached Node.js runtime
- ui-deps: Cached UI dependencies (npm packages)
- runtime-base: Cached Alpine runtime setup

Expected performance: ~2-3x faster builds with warm cache, near-instant
with hot cache. Each layer is checked individually and reused if available.

* fix: remove unused gitCommit variable in BaseWithCache

Move git commit retrieval to PackageWithCache where it's actually used
for the ldflags. Fixes build error: declared and not used: gitCommit

* chore: trigger CI to test cache

Signed-off-by: Mark Phelps <209477+markphelps@users.noreply.github.com>

* fix: mount node_modules cache in UI cached dependencies path

When using cached UI dependencies, we still need to mount the node_modules
cache volume so that installed packages (like tsc) are available for the
build process. Fixes 'tsc: not found' error in CI.

* fix: simplify UI caching to use cache volumes for dependencies

Registry caching doesn't work well for npm dependencies because the
installed packages are in cache volumes, not in the container layers.
Switched to:
- Registry cache for Node.js base image only
- Cache volumes for npm dependencies (more reliable and efficient)
- Removed ui-deps cache references from CI workflow

This approach provides the base image caching benefit while ensuring
npm dependencies are properly accessible via cache volumes.

* fix: use cache volumes for Go dependencies instead of registry caching

Registry caching doesn't work well for Go modules because they are stored
in cache volumes (/go/pkg/mod and /root/.cache/go-build), not in container
filesystem layers. Switched to:
- Registry cache for golang-base image only
- Cache volumes for Go modules and build cache (more reliable and efficient)
- Removed golang-deps cache references from CI workflow

This approach provides the base image caching benefit while ensuring
Go modules are properly cached via volumes, eliminating the ~2min module
download time during builds.

fix: implement simple, reliable version detection using /releases/latest

The root cause of I/O errors was storing large API responses (2.15MB) in shell
variables. The solution uses a much simpler approach:

## Key Changes:
1. **Use /releases/latest endpoint**: Avoids rate limiting issues with /releases
2. **Pipeline processing only**: Never store large responses in variables
3. **Simple validation**: Check if latest release is v2.x, use it directly
4. **Multiple fallback paths**: jq method -> grep method -> recent releases search
5. **Eliminate complexity**: No need for complex sorting since latest = newest

## Why This Works:
- /releases/latest doesn't hit rate limits like /releases
- Currently v2.0.0 is the only stable v2 release and shows as latest
- When v2.1.0+ is released, it will automatically become latest
- Handles both jq available and jq unavailable environments
- Works with limited CI tokens and without tokens locally

## Testing:
✅ Local testing: Correctly detects v2.0.0 and starts installation
✅ No shell compatibility issues (POSIX compliant)
✅ No I/O errors with pipeline processing
✅ Graceful fallbacks for different environments

This approach is much more reliable and maintainable than complex
sorting/filtering of large API responses.

fix: comprehensive Keygen API rate limit handling improvements (#4602)

* fix: improve Keygen API rate limit handling with caching and proper error types

Comprehensive fix for Keygen API rate limit issues during pod restarts:

1. **License Caching**: Cache successful validations for 6 hours to reduce API calls
2. **Proper Error Types**: Use keygen-go library error types instead of string matching
3. **Rate Limit Detection**: Detect rate limits using RateLimitError type
4. **Permanent Error Handling**: Stop retries for permanent errors like FINGERPRINT_SCOPE_MISMATCH
5. **Startup Delay**: Random 0-30s delay to prevent thundering herd
6. **Extended Revalidation**: Increased interval from 12h to 24h
7. **Graceful Degradation**: Keep Pro features with cached license during rate limits

This should significantly reduce API calls and prevent hitting the 1,000 daily request limit.

Fixes rate limiting issues seen during pod crash/restart scenarios.

Signed-off-by: Mark Phelps <209477+markphelps@users.noreply.github.com>

* refactor: improve keygen-go error handling with proper error types

Clean up error handling to use proper keygen-go library error types:

1. **RateLimitError Type**: Use keygen.RateLimitError instead of string matching
2. **Proper Error Mapping**: Leverage keygen-go client's built-in error code mapping
3. **Intelligent Rate Limit Reset**: Track actual reset time from RateLimitError
4. **Enhanced Logging**: Include rate limit details (retry_after, remaining, reset_at)
5. **Simplified Logic**: Remove redundant string matching and API error code handling

The keygen-go client already properly maps all API error codes to typed errors,
so we can rely on errors.Is() and errors.As() for clean, reliable error handling.

This makes rate limit detection more precise and reduces the likelihood of false positives.

fix: handle empty directories correctly during namespace deletion (#4622)

* fix: handle empty directories correctly during namespace deletion

This fixes issue #4621 where Bitbucket returns 500 errors after rapid
namespace deletion operations through the Flipt GUI.

The issue was caused by improper handling of empty Git tree objects when
directories became empty after file deletion. The fix includes:

- Properly remove empty directories from parent tree after deletion
- Handle empty tree objects with well-known hash
- Add tree validation before encoding
- Ensure tree objects are properly stored before creating commits
- Add comprehensive tests for rapid namespace deletion scenarios

The core issue was that when all files were deleted from a directory,
the directory itself wasn't being removed from the parent tree, leaving
invalid tree objects that Bitbucket couldn't parse.

Fixes #4621

feat: support Git repository initialization for existing features files

This commit implements automatic Git repository detection and initialization for
existing features.yaml files when using local storage backend. This addresses
the common user workflow where they have existing feature flag configurations
but no Git repository initialized yet.

Key changes:
- Enhanced repository detection logic to distinguish between normal Git repos
  (with .git subdirectory) and bare repositories (Git files in root)
- Added support for opening existing normal Git repositories created by users
- Automatic remote tracking reference setup for normal repositories to ensure
  Flipt's branch management works correctly
- Working directory synchronization for normal repos - changes in UI now update
  the actual .yaml files on disk
- Comprehensive test suite covering all repository initialization scenarios

User workflow now supported:
```bash
# User can create features and initialize Git manually
mkdir -p flags/production
cp existing-features.yaml flags/production/features.yaml
cd flags && git init && git add . && git commit -m "Initial features"
# Then run Flipt - it will detect and work with the normal repository
```

The implementation maintains backward compatibility with existing bare repository
workflows while adding support for the more intuitive normal repository approach
that users expect from standard Git workflows.

Fixes #4589

* fix(git): enable pruning when fetching to remove deleted remote branches

Added Prune: true to FetchOptions to ensure deleted remote branches
are removed from local tracking refs. Without this, when a branch is
deleted upstream, the local ref refs/remotes/origin/branch-name persists,
causing the branch to still appear as existing in Git.

to show in the Flipt UI. The branch detection logic scans refs/remotes/origin/*
refs, and without pruning, deleted upstream branches remain in the
local repository indefinitely.

allowing RefreshEnvironment to correctly detect and remove deleted branches.

fix(build): update Dagger build to work without go.work files (#4817)

* fix(build): update Dagger build to work without go.work files

The Dagger base image build was parsing go.work and go.work.sum files
to determine which module dependency files to mount. Since these workspace
files were removed from version control (being local-dev only), the build
process now mounts dependency files directly based on the replace directives
in go.mod.

Changes:
- Mount root go.mod and go.sum directly instead of go.work files
- Explicitly mount submodule dependency files (core, errors, rpc/*, sdk/go)
- Remove unused golang.org/x/mod/modfile import
- Support both v1 (4 submodules) and v2 (6 submodules) module structures

Signed-off-by: Mark Phelps <209477+markphelps@users.noreply.github.com>

* fix(build): add missing build and sdk/go/v2 submodules to Dagger mount

The Dagger build process needs to mount go.mod and go.sum files for all
submodules that have replace directives. The build module and sdk/go/v2
submodule were missing from the list, causing go mod download to fail
when running tests that depend on the build module.

This adds both missing submodules to ensure their dependencies are
properly downloaded before the test phase.

Fixes the unit test failure where go run ./build/internal/cmd/gitea/...
could not find the build module.

Signed-off-by: Mark Phelps <209477+markphelps@users.noreply.github.com>

* fix(build): create go.work file in container for multi-module support

The Dagger build container needs a go.work file to support running
commands across multiple Go modules (main module and submodules like
build, core, errors, etc.).

Without go.work, commands like 'go run ./build/internal/cmd/gitea/...'
fail because Go doesn't recognize build as part of the workspace and
treats it as an external module that's not in the dependency graph.

This change dynamically creates a go.work file in the container after
mounting the full project, enabling the workspace mode that allows
tests to run commands in submodules while maintaining access to the
main module's resources.

* fix(build): run go work sync after creating workspace file

Add 'go work sync' command after creating go.work to ensure the
workspace is properly initialized. This:

- Generates go.work.sum file which may be required
- Validates the workspace configuration
- Ensures all workspace modules are properly recognized

This should fix the 'directory prefix build/internal/cmd/discover does
not contain main module or its selected dependencies' error.

Signed-off-by: Mark Phelps <209477+markphelps@users.noreply.github.com>

* fix(build): download workspace module dependencies after workspace creation

The root cause of the 'does not contain main module or its selected
dependencies' error was that we only downloaded dependencies for the
main module before creating the workspace.

The build module (and other workspace modules) need their dependencies
downloaded too. The fix is to run 'go mod download' AFTER creating the
workspace, which downloads dependencies for ALL workspace modules.

Sequence now:
1. Download main module deps (before workspace)
2. Mount full project
3. Create go.work workspace
4. Sync workspace (generates go.work.sum)
5. Download ALL workspace module deps (now workspace is active)

This ensures 'go run ./build/internal/cmd/discover/...' has access to
all required dependencies.

* fix(build): setup Go workspace in cached test runner container

The lightweight test runner container used when cachedImage is provided

This adds the same workspace setup logic to the cached test runner

feat: add custom commit and PR templates in server config (#5091)

* feat: add custom commit and PR templates in server config

Add support for configuring commit message and pull request templates
at the server configuration level. This allows operators to define
server-wide default templates that can be used when creating commits
and pull requests through the Flipt UI.

Templates are configured per storage backend and support:
- commit_message: Template for commit messages
- proposal_title: Template for pull request titles
- proposal_body: Template for pull request body content

Template priority (highest to lowest):
1. Repository-level templates (in flipt.yaml)
2. Server-level templates (in config.yml storage section)
3. Built-in defaults

This is useful for CI/CD integration, such as adding [skip ci]
to commit messages to prevent unnecessary pipeline triggers.

Example configuration:
  storage:
    default:
      templates:
        commit_message: "{{ (index .Changes 0) }} [skip ci]"

Fixes flipt-io/flipt#5087

Signed-off-by: Mark Phelps <209477+markphelps@users.noreply.github.com>

* fix: add early validation for template configuration

Add TemplatesConfig.Validate() method to check that all configured
templates are valid Go text/templates at config load time. This
provides clear error messages at startup rather than silently
falling back to defaults when a template has a syntax error.

- Added Validate() method to TemplatesConfig in internal/config/storage.go
- Call validation from StorageConfig.validate() during config load
- Added comprehensive tests for template validation
- Updated documentation in DefaultFliptConfig to clarify graceful degradation

Signed-off-by: Mark Phelps <209477+markphelps@users.noreply.github.com>

* fix: add templates property to storage schema

Add the templates property to the JSON schema for storage configuration.
This allows the schema validation test to pass when using the new
templates configuration option.

Signed-off-by: Mark Phelps <209477+markphelps@users.noreply.github.com>

* fix: add templates property to Cue schema

Add the templates property to the Cue schema for storage configuration,
matching the JSON schema update.

Signed-off-by: Mark Phelps <209477+markphelps@users.noreply.github.com>

* refactor: move templates config to root level and use value types

Address code review feedback:
1. Move TemplatesConfig from per-storage to root config level since

2. Change DefaultFliptConfig and related functions to accept value

   longer related to storage configuration
4. Update JSON and Cue schemas to reflect templates at root level
5. Fix JSON tags to use camelCase convention

fix: resolve secrets in OIDC provider configuration (#5153)

* fix: resolve secrets in OIDC provider configuration

Map values obtained from MapIndex() are non-addressable in Go's reflection API,
preventing secret references from being resolved in the walkConfigForSecrets
function. This fix creates an addressable copy of struct map values, resolves
secrets in the copy, and sets the modified value back into the map.

This enables using ${secret:file:...} syntax in OIDC provider credentials
configuration (client_id and client_secret fields).

Fixes #5131

fix(git): complete ref update after fetch for both bare and normal repositories (#5144)

* fix(git): complete ref update after fetch for both bare and normal repositories

The Fetch method was not persisting fetched references to refs/heads after
pulling from the remote. When using depth=1 (shallow fetches), the shallow
boundary wasn't maintained and refs/heads/ were never created. For normal repos
with full history, updatedRefs were collected but never written to storage.

- For shallow repositories: Create refs/heads/ and maintain shallow boundary
- For normal repositories: Create refs/heads/ from updatedRefs
- Ensure both code paths properly persist fetched references to local storage

Signed-off-by: Roman Dmytrenko <rdmytrenko@gmail.com>

feat(oidc): support configurable token signing algorithms (#5362)

Some OIDC providers sign ID tokens with non-RS256 algorithms. Add an `algorithms`
setting to the OIDC provider config and plumb it through to the OIDC client
configuration. Default remains ["RS256"] for backward compatibility.

Signed-off-by: Edward Xu <edwardx@nvidia.com>

feat(oidc): optionally merge userinfo claims into auth session (#5364)

Some OIDC providers keep ID token claims minimal and require calling the
UserInfo endpoint to obtain additional attributes, especially when the
group list is long.

This patch adds an `include_user_info` provider option to fetch UserInfo
during the callback flow and merge returned claims into the existing claim
set.

The default remains false to preserve existing behavior.

This patch also removed unused UserInfo mocks from old tests.

feat: rewrite v1 install script with robust version detection

Complete rewrite of the main branch install script to match the v2 version
but adapted for v1-only releases:

**Major improvements:**
- Robust v1-only version detection using /releases endpoint with JSON parsing
- Filters out prereleases, drafts, and v2 releases entirely
- Structured logging with color-coded info/warn/error messages
- Modular platform detection functions (OS and architecture)
- Enhanced error handling and user feedback
- Flexible installation directory support via BIN_DIR environment variable
- POSIX-compliant (no 'local' keywords, passes shellcheck)

**v1-specific behavior:**
- Only accepts and installs v1.x.x releases
- Explicitly rejects v2.x.x versions with clear error message
- Finds latest stable v1 release even if newer v2 releases exist
- Uses same robust JSON parsing as v2 script but filters for v1

**Future-proof design:**
- Will continue to install latest stable v1 release regardless of v2 releases
- Properly excludes beta/alpha/rc versions by checking GitHub's prerelease flag
- Resilient to GitHub API changes with comprehensive error handling

**Testing verified:**
- ✅ Installs latest v1.59.2 release correctly
- ✅ Rejects v2.0.0 with clear error message
- ✅ Installs specific v1 versions (e.g., v1.59.0)
- ✅ Passes shellcheck with no warnings
- ✅ Cross-platform compatibility

This provides v1 users with the same robust, user-friendly installation
experience as the v2 script while maintaining strict v1-only behavior.

Signed-off-by: Mark Phelps <209477+markphelps@users.noreply.github.com>

fix: correct architecture naming in v1 install script

Changes x86_64 architecture detection from 'amd64' to 'x86_64' to match
actual Flipt release file naming convention. Release files use
flipt_{os}_x86_64.tar.gz format, not flipt_{os}_amd64.tar.gz.

Fixes download URL generation that was causing 404 errors when
installing on x86_64 systems.

feat(metrics): add Git sync observability metrics to feature flag backend (#4673)

* This change enhances Flipt's Git-based feature flag backend observability by adding detailed synchronization metrics. Currently, failures during Git sync are only logged without metric visibility, limiting proactive monitoring and alerting capabilities.

    - Introduce new OpenTelemetry metrics for Git sync operations:
      - Last sync time as an observable gauge (timestamp).
      - Sync duration histogram.
      - Counters for number of flags fetched.
      - Success and failure counts with failure reason attributes.

    - Instrument the `SnapshotStore.update` method, the core sync loop, to record these metrics accurately on every sync attempt, including partial failures and cleanups.

    - Extend the `Snapshot` type with `TotalFlagsCount()` to count all flags across namespaces for metric reporting.

    - Integrate metrics initialization in app startup ensuring consistent telemetry setup.

    - Improve test coverage by suggesting strategies to verify metric emission and sync behavior.

    These metric additions enable operators to monitor Git sync health, detect failures promptly, and troubleshoot issues efficiently, significantly improving runtime observability and system reliability.

fix: uts after removing go.work* (#4816)

* fix: uts after removing go.work*

Signed-off-by: Mark Phelps <209477+markphelps@users.noreply.github.com>

* chore: fix go.sum files

Signed-off-by: Mark Phelps <209477+markphelps@users.noreply.github.com>

* chore: mod tidy

Signed-off-by: Mark Phelps <209477+markphelps@users.noreply.github.com>

* fix: add go.work setup to build container for migration tests

The migration tests were failing because the build container was missing
the go.work file needed for multi-module workspace support. After the
removal of go.work files from the repository, the container needs to:

1. Create a go.work file with all workspace modules
2. Run 'go work sync' to generate go.work.sum
3. Run 'go mod download' to fetch dependencies for all modules

This ensures that tests which run commands in submodules (like the
readonly integration tests) can properly resolve dependencies.

Fixes the "FAIL go.flipt.io/build/testing/integration/readonly [setup failed]"
error in CI.

Signed-off-by: Mark Phelps <209477+markphelps@users.noreply.github.com>

* fix: recreate go.work after mounting cloned release in migration test

The migration test clones an older Flipt release and mounts it over the
current directory, which replaces the go.work file created in the base
container. This causes go.sum validation errors when running tests from
the cloned release.

Fix by recreating the go.work file and re-running workspace sync and
dependency download after mounting the cloned release directory.

This ensures the cloned release's go.mod files have their dependencies
properly downloaded and validated.

Signed-off-by: Mark Phelps <209477+markphelps@users.noreply.github.com>

fix(license): resolve timeout issues during license deactivation on shutdown (#4486)

* fix(license): resolve timeout issues during license deactivation on shutdown

The license manager was experiencing timeout errors during shutdown when
attempting to deactivate licenses with the Keygen API. This occurred due
to two issues:

1. No explicit timeout on the HTTP client, causing requests to hang
   indefinitely when the Keygen API was slow or unreachable
2. License deactivation competing with other shutdown operations for
   the shared 30-second shutdown context

Changes:
- Add 10-second timeout to retryable HTTP client for Keygen API calls
- Reduce retry attempts from 5 to 3 for faster failure detection
- Use dedicated 15-second timeout context for license deactivation
- Prevent deactivation from being cancelled by other shutdown operations

This ensures license deactivation completes within a reasonable timeframe
while maintaining graceful shutdown behavior and allowing licenses to be
properly released for use on other machines.

Fixes the "context deadline exceeded" error during application shutdown.

The --cases flag should be passed to the integration subcommand, not the test-with-cache command.

* fix: ensure cached image reference is always populated

The cache image output was empty when cache hit occurred because we were only setting
the image reference conditionally. Now we always set the expected image reference
regardless of cache hit/miss status.

Signed-off-by: Mark Phelps <209477+markphelps@users.noreply.github.com>

* fix: remove unused IMAGE_REF variable

Clean up the shell script by directly using the env vars instead of an intermediate variable.

Signed-off-by: Mark Phelps <209477+markphelps@users.noreply.github.com>

* docs: add registry cache optimization details to build/CLAUDE.md

Document the new caching approach including:
- Registry cache strategy and workflow
- Performance benefits and expected improvements
- Cache management and troubleshooting
- New Dagger cache-related functions
- Debug commands for cache issues

Signed-off-by: Mark Phelps <209477+markphelps@users.noreply.github.com>

* fix: use lightweight base container when using cached images

The TestWithCache function was still rebuilding the full base container from scratch,
defeating the purpose of the cache optimization. Now when using cached images:

- Use lightweight test runner (golang:1.24-alpine3.21 + basic tools)
- Skip expensive Go build environment setup
- Only mount source code needed for test execution

This should significantly improve the cache performance in CI.

Signed-off-by: Mark Phelps <209477+markphelps@users.noreply.github.com>

* chore: rm --race for ITs

Signed-off-by: Mark Phelps <209477+markphelps@users.noreply.github.com>

* feat: optimize container builds with multi-layered registry caching

Implement comprehensive build optimization using registry-backed caching
for all build stages to dramatically reduce CI build times.

- golang-base: Cached Go toolchain with build dependencies
- golang-deps: Cached Go module dependencies
- node-base: Cached Node.js runtime
- ui-deps: Cached UI dependencies (npm packages)
- runtime-base: Cached Alpine runtime setup

Expected performance: ~2-3x faster builds with warm cache, near-instant
with hot cache. Each layer is checked individually and reused if available.

* fix: remove unused gitCommit variable in BaseWithCache

Move git commit retrieval to PackageWithCache where it's actually used
for the ldflags. Fixes build error: declared and not used: gitCommit

* chore: trigger CI to test cache

Signed-off-by: Mark Phelps <209477+markphelps@users.noreply.github.com>

* fix: mount node_modules cache in UI cached dependencies path

When using cached UI dependencies, we still need to mount the node_modules
cache volume so that installed packages (like tsc) are available for the
build process. Fixes 'tsc: not found' error in CI.

* fix: simplify UI caching to use cache volumes for dependencies

Registry caching doesn't work well for npm dependencies because the
installed packages are in cache volumes, not in the container layers.
Switched to:
- Registry cache for Node.js base image only
- Cache volumes for npm dependencies (more reliable and efficient)
- Removed ui-deps cache references from CI workflow

This approach provides the base image caching benefit while ensuring
npm dependencies are properly accessible via cache volumes.

* fix: use cache volumes for Go dependencies instead of registry caching

Registry caching doesn't work well for Go modules because they are stored
in cache volumes (/go/pkg/mod and /root/.cache/go-build), not in container
filesystem layers. Switched to:
- Registry cache for golang-base image only
- Cache volumes for Go modules and build cache (more reliable and efficient)
- Removed golang-deps cache references from CI workflow

This approach provides the base image caching benefit while ensuring
Go modules are properly cached via volumes, eliminating the ~2min module
download time during builds.

fix: implement simple, reliable version detection using /releases/latest

The root cause of I/O errors was storing large API responses (2.15MB) in shell
variables. The solution uses a much simpler approach:

## Key Changes:
1. **Use /releases/latest endpoint**: Avoids rate limiting issues with /releases
2. **Pipeline processing only**: Never store large responses in variables
3. **Simple validation**: Check if latest release is v2.x, use it directly
4. **Multiple fallback paths**: jq method -> grep method -> recent releases search
5. **Eliminate complexity**: No need for complex sorting since latest = newest

## Why This Works:
- /releases/latest doesn't hit rate limits like /releases
- Currently v2.0.0 is the only stable v2 release and shows as latest
- When v2.1.0+ is released, it will automatically become latest
- Handles both jq available and jq unavailable environments
- Works with limited CI tokens and without tokens locally

## Testing:
✅ Local testing: Correctly detects v2.0.0 and starts installation
✅ No shell compatibility issues (POSIX compliant)
✅ No I/O errors with pipeline processing
✅ Graceful fallbacks for different environments

This approach is much more reliable and maintainable than complex
sorting/filtering of large API responses.

fix: comprehensive Keygen API rate limit handling improvements (#4602)

* fix: improve Keygen API rate limit handling with caching and proper error types

Comprehensive fix for Keygen API rate limit issues during pod restarts:

1. **License Caching**: Cache successful validations for 6 hours to reduce API calls
2. **Proper Error Types**: Use keygen-go library error types instead of string matching
3. **Rate Limit Detection**: Detect rate limits using RateLimitError type
4. **Permanent Error Handling**: Stop retries for permanent errors like FINGERPRINT_SCOPE_MISMATCH
5. **Startup Delay**: Random 0-30s delay to prevent thundering herd
6. **Extended Revalidation**: Increased interval from 12h to 24h
7. **Graceful Degradation**: Keep Pro features with cached license during rate limits

This should significantly reduce API calls and prevent hitting the 1,000 daily request limit.

Fixes rate limiting issues seen during pod crash/restart scenarios.

Signed-off-by: Mark Phelps <209477+markphelps@users.noreply.github.com>

* refactor: improve keygen-go error handling with proper error types

Clean up error handling to use proper keygen-go library error types:

1. **RateLimitError Type**: Use keygen.RateLimitError instead of string matching
2. **Proper Error Mapping**: Leverage keygen-go client's built-in error code mapping
3. **Intelligent Rate Limit Reset**: Track actual reset time from RateLimitError
4. **Enhanced Logging**: Include rate limit details (retry_after, remaining, reset_at)
5. **Simplified Logic**: Remove redundant string matching and API error code handling

The keygen-go client already properly maps all API error codes to typed errors,
so we can rely on errors.Is() and errors.As() for clean, reliable error handling.

This makes rate limit detection more precise and reduces the likelihood of false positives.

fix: handle empty directories correctly during namespace deletion (#4622)

* fix: handle empty directories correctly during namespace deletion

This fixes issue #4621 where Bitbucket returns 500 errors after rapid
namespace deletion operations through the Flipt GUI.

The issue was caused by improper handling of empty Git tree objects when
directories became empty after file deletion. The fix includes:

- Properly remove empty directories from parent tree after deletion
- Handle empty tree objects with well-known hash
- Add tree validation before encoding
- Ensure tree objects are properly stored before creating commits
- Add comprehensive tests for rapid namespace deletion scenarios

The core issue was that when all files were deleted from a directory,
the directory itself wasn't being removed from the parent tree, leaving
invalid tree objects that Bitbucket couldn't parse.

Fixes #4621

feat: support Git repository initialization for existing features files

This commit implements automatic Git repository detection and initialization for
existing features.yaml files when using local storage backend. This addresses
the common user workflow where they have existing feature flag configurations
but no Git repository initialized yet.

Key changes:
- Enhanced repository detection logic to distinguish between normal Git repos
  (with .git subdirectory) and bare repositories (Git files in root)
- Added support for opening existing normal Git repositories created by users
- Automatic remote tracking reference setup for normal repositories to ensure
  Flipt's branch management works correctly
- Working directory synchronization for normal repos - changes in UI now update
  the actual .yaml files on disk
- Comprehensive test suite covering all repository initialization scenarios

User workflow now supported:
```bash
# User can create features and initialize Git manually
mkdir -p flags/production
cp existing-features.yaml flags/production/features.yaml
cd flags && git init && git add . && git commit -m "Initial features"
# Then run Flipt - it will detect and work with the normal repository
```

The implementation maintains backward compatibility with existing bare repository
workflows while adding support for the more intuitive normal repository approach
that users expect from standard Git workflows.

Fixes #4589

* fix(git): enable pruning when fetching to remove deleted remote branches

Added Prune: true to FetchOptions to ensure deleted remote branches
are removed from local tracking refs. Without this, when a branch is
deleted upstream, the local ref refs/remotes/origin/branch-name persists,
causing the branch to still appear as existing in Git.

to show in the Flipt UI. The branch detection logic scans refs/remotes/origin/*
refs, and without pruning, deleted upstream branches remain in the
local repository indefinitely.

With pruning enabled, git fetch will remove stale tracking branches,
allowing RefreshEnvironment to correctly detect and remove deleted branches.

fix(build): update Dagger build to work without go.work files (#4817)

* fix(build): update Dagger build to work without go.work files

The Dagger base image build was parsing go.work and go.work.sum files
to determine which module dependency files to mount. Since these workspace
files were removed from version control (being local-dev only), the build
process now mounts dependency files directly based on the replace directives
in go.mod.

Changes:
- Mount root go.mod and go.sum directly instead of go.work files
- Explicitly mount submodule dependency files (core, errors, rpc/*, sdk/go)
- Remove unused golang.org/x/mod/modfile import
- Support both v1 (4 submodules) and v2 (6 submodules) module structures

Signed-off-by: Mark Phelps <209477+markphelps@users.noreply.github.com>

* fix(build): add missing build and sdk/go/v2 submodules to Dagger mount

The Dagger build process needs to mount go.mod and go.sum files for all
submodules that have replace directives. The build module and sdk/go/v2
submodule were missing from the list, causing go mod download to fail
when running tests that depend on the build module.

This adds both missing submodules to ensure their dependencies are
properly downloaded before the test phase.

Fixes the unit test failure where go run ./build/internal/cmd/gitea/...
could not find the build module.

Signed-off-by: Mark Phelps <209477+markphelps@users.noreply.github.com>

* fix(build): create go.work file in container for multi-module support

The Dagger build container needs a go.work file to support running
commands across multiple Go modules (main module and submodules like
build, core, errors, etc.).

Without go.work, commands like 'go run ./build/internal/cmd/gitea/...'
fail because Go doesn't recognize build as part of the workspace and
treats it as an external module that's not in the dependency graph.

This change dynamically creates a go.work file in the container after
mounting the full project, enabling the workspace mode that allows
tests to run commands in submodules while maintaining access to the
main module's resources.

Signed-off-by: Mark Phelps <209477+markphelps@users.noreply.github.com>

refactor(build): use static go.work.container file instead of dynamic generation (#4818)

* refactor(build): use static go.work.container file instead of dynamic generation

Replace dynamic go.work file generation with a static go.work.container
file that gets copied into the Dagger build container. This approach:

- Makes the workspace configuration explicit and version-controlled
- Simplifies the build code by removing multi-line string generation
- Makes it easier to maintain the list of workspace modules
- Provides better visibility into what modules are in the workspace

The .container suffix prevents this file from being picked up during
local development where developers may want their own go.work files.

Signed-off-by: Mark Phelps <209477+markphelps@users.noreply.github.com>

* fix(ci): suppress SIGPIPE error in cache key generation

When find outputs more than 20 files, head -20 closes the pipe after
reading 20 lines, causing find to receive SIGPIPE and exit with error.
This results in 'Broken pipe' and 'write error' messages in the CI logs.

Add 2>/dev/null to suppress the expected SIGPIPE error while still
maintaining the correct cache key generation behavior.

Signed-off-by: Mark Phelps <209477+markphelps@users.noreply.github.com>

* fix(build): inline go.work content instead of copying from file

The source.File() approach for copying go.work.container was failing in
CI, likely due to mount ordering issues or file not being found in the
source directory.

Revert to inlining the go.work content directly in the code to ensure
it's always available. Keep the go.work.container file as documentation
of the workspace configuration.

Signed-off-by: Mark Phelps <209477+markphelps@users.noreply.github.com>

* fix(build): run go work sync after creating workspace file

Add 'go work sync' command after creating go.work to ensure the
workspace is properly initialized. This:

- Generates go.work.sum file which may be required
- Validates the workspace configuration
- Ensures all workspace modules are properly recognized

This should fix the 'directory prefix build/internal/cmd/discover does
not contain main module or its selected dependencies' error.

Signed-off-by: Mark Phelps <209477+markphelps@users.noreply.github.com>

* fix(build): download workspace module dependencies after workspace creation

The root cause of the 'does not contain main module or its selected
dependencies' error was that we only downloaded dependencies for the
main module before creating the workspace.

The build module (and other workspace modules) need their dependencies
downloaded too. The fix is to run 'go mod download' AFTER creating the
workspace, which downloads dependencies for ALL workspace modules.

Sequence now:
1. Download main module deps (before workspace)
2. Mount full project
3. Create go.work workspace
4. Sync workspace (generates go.work.sum)
5. Download ALL workspace module deps (now workspace is active)

This ensures 'go run ./build/internal/cmd/discover/...' has access to
all required dependencies.

Signed-off-by: Mark Phelps <209477+markphelps@users.noreply.github.com>

* fix(build): setup Go workspace in cached test runner container

The lightweight test runner container used when cachedImage is provided
was missing the Go workspace setup, causing integration tests to fail
when trying to run commands in submodules (e.g., go run ./build/internal/cmd/gitea/...).

This adds the same workspace setup logic to the cached test runner
that was already present in the Base() function:
- Creates go.work file with all submodules
- Runs go work sync to validate workspace
- Runs go mod download to fetch all workspace module dependencies

referenced by flag rules or rollouts. This ensures data integrity by
checking all flags in the namespace before allowing segment deletion.

Signed-off-by: Roman Dmytrenko <rdmytrenko@gmail.com>

fix(ui): prevent Enter key from submitting form in Tags component (#4896)

Modified the Tags input component to always prevent the default
Enter key behavior (form submission), regardless of whether the
input has a value. This fixes the issue where pressing Enter in
the Values textbox for "IS ONE OF" or "IS NOT ONE OF" constraints
would save the entire form instead of just adding a tag.

The Enter key now:
- Always prevents form submission
- Adds a tag only when the input field has a value
- Does nothing when the input is empty

Fixes #4894

Signed-off-by: Mark Phelps <209477+markphelps@users.noreply.github.com>
Co-authored-by: Roman Dmytrenko <rdmytrenko@gmail.com>

* fix: prevent install script failure with TERM=dumb

actually execute successfully before attempting to set color variables.

feat: add custom commit and PR templates in server config (#5091)

* feat: add custom commit and PR templates in server config

Add support for configuring commit message and pull request templates
at the server configuration level. This allows operators to define
server-wide default templates that can be used when creating commits
and pull requests through the Flipt UI.

Templates are configured per storage backend and support:
- commit_message: Template for commit messages
- proposal_title: Template for pull request titles
- proposal_body: Template for pull request body content

Template priority (highest to lowest):
1. Repository-level templates (in flipt.yaml)
2. Server-level templates (in config.yml storage section)
3. Built-in defaults

This is useful for CI/CD integration, such as adding [skip ci]
to commit messages to prevent unnecessary pipeline triggers.

Example configuration:
  storage:
    default:
      templates:
        commit_message: "{{ (index .Changes 0) }} [skip ci]"

Fixes flipt-io/flipt#5087

Signed-off-by: Mark Phelps <209477+markphelps@users.noreply.github.com>

* fix: add early validation for template configuration

Add TemplatesConfig.Validate() method to check that all configured
templates are valid Go text/templates at config load time. This
provides clear error messages at startup rather than silently
falling back to defaults when a template has a syntax error.

- Added Validate() method to TemplatesConfig in internal/config/storage.go
- Call validation from StorageConfig.validate() during config load
- Added comprehensive tests for template validation
- Updated documentation in DefaultFliptConfig to clarify graceful degradation

Signed-off-by: Mark Phelps <209477+markphelps@users.noreply.github.com>

* fix: add templates property to storage schema

Add the templates property to the JSON schema for storage configuration.
This allows the schema validation test to pass when using the new
templates configuration option.

Add the templates property to the Cue schema for storage configuration,

fix: resolve secrets in OIDC provider configuration (#5153)

* fix: resolve secrets in OIDC provider configuration

Map values obtained from MapIndex() are non-addressable in Go's reflection API,
preventing secret references from being resolved in the walkConfigForSecrets
function. This fix creates an addressable copy of struct map values, resolves
secrets in the copy, and sets the modified value back into the map.

This enables using ${secret:file:...} syntax in OIDC provider credentials
configuration (client_id and client_secret fields).

Fixes #5131

fix(git): complete ref update after fetch for both bare and normal repositories (#5144)

* fix(git): complete ref update after fetch for both bare and normal repositories

The Fetch method was not persisting fetched references to refs/heads after
pulling from the remote. When using depth=1 (shallow fetches), the shallow
boundary wasn't maintained and refs/heads/ were never created. For normal repos
with full history, updatedRefs were collected but never written to storage.

- For shallow repositories: Create refs/heads/ and maintain shallow boundary
- For normal repositories: Create refs/heads/ from updatedRefs
- Ensure both code paths properly persist fetched references to local storage

Signed-off-by: Roman Dmytrenko <rdmytrenko@gmail.com>

feat(oidc): support configurable token signing algorithms (#5362)

Some OIDC providers sign ID tokens with non-RS256 algorithms. Add an `algorithms`
setting to the OIDC provider config and plumb it through to the OIDC client
configuration. Default remains ["RS256"] for backward compatibility.

Signed-off-by: Edward Xu <edwardx@nvidia.com>

feat(oidc): optionally merge userinfo claims into auth session (#5364)

Some OIDC providers keep ID token claims minimal and require calling the
UserInfo endpoint to obtain additional attributes, especially when the
group list is long.

This patch adds an `include_user_info` provider option to fetch UserInfo
during the callback flow and merge returned claims into the existing claim
set.

The default remains false to preserve existing behavior.

This patch also removed unused UserInfo mocks from old tests.

* feat(secrets): add Azure Key Vault provider

Add Azure Key Vault as a secret provider for Flipt, following the same
patterns as the existing GCP and AWS providers.

- Add AzureProviderConfig with vault_url field and validation
- Implement provider using Azure SDK (azidentity + azsecrets)
- Support emulator mode via AZURE_KEYVAULT_EMULATOR env var
- Wire provider into secrets manager and main.go
- Add CUE and JSON schema entries
- Add unit tests for config, provider, manager, and secret resolution
- Add integration test using Lowkey Vault emulator

Signed-off-by: Mark Phelps <209477+markphelps@users.noreply.github.com>

* fix(secrets): fix go mod tidy and Lowkey Vault image tag

- Run go mod tidy to clean up dependencies

Signed-off-by: Mark Phelps <209477+markphelps@users.noreply.github.com>

* fix(secrets): disable challenge resource verification for Azure emulator

The Azure SDK validates that the challenge resource URL matches the
requested domain, which fails with the Lowkey Vault emulator. Set
DisableChallengeResourceVerification to true in emulator mode.

Signed-off-by: Mark Phelps <209477+markphelps@users.noreply.github.com>

* fix(secrets): register vault alias for Lowkey Vault emulator hostname

The Lowkey Vault emulator creates vaults at https://<name>.localhost:<port>
by default, but the Dagger service binding exposes it as "lowkey-vault".
Register a vault alias so the emulator recognizes requests to
https://lowkey-vault:8443 as a valid vault URI.

Fixes "Unable to find active vault: https://lowkey-vault:8443" error
in the signing/azure integration test.

chore: migrate goreleaser configs to dockers_v2 and homebrew_casks (#5508)

Replace deprecated `dockers` + `docker_manifests` with `dockers_v2` in
both `.goreleaser.yml` and `.goreleaser.nightly.yml`. The new config
produces identical multi-arch Docker images and manifests with
significantly less boilerplate.

Replace deprecated `brews` with `homebrew_casks` in `.goreleaser.yml`.
Binary installation uses the cask-native `binaries` field. Shell
completions, the Homebrew service definition, and post_install log
directory creation are dropped — these formula-specific features need
different approaches in casks (e.g. pre-generated completion files in
the archive, launchd plists) and can be added as follow-ups.

Closes #5503

feat: normalize rollout distribution buckets (#5581)

Port rollout bucket logic from Rust client to Go server.

Previously, bucket boundaries were calculated by directly accumulating
rollout percentages. Now, each distribution's rollout is normalized
relative to the total rollout sum, ensuring proportional bucket
distribution even when distributions don't sum to 100.

The last bucket is always set to totalBucketNum (1000) to ensure
complete coverage of the bucket space.

fix(stream): don't suppress digest reverts in snapshot stream (#5923)

* fix(stream): skip initial snapshot only, not reverts to original digest

The digest check r.GetDigest() == snap.GetDigest() was meant to suppress
the first snapshot when the client already has that state. However it also
suppressed any later snapshot whose digest happened to equal the original
request digest (e.g. after a git rollback), leaving clients stuck on stale
data indefinitely.

Guard the check with lastDigest == nil so it only fires before the first
update is sent; subsequent deduplication is handled by the existing
hash-based comparison.

Signed-off-by: Immanuel Tikhonov <pchpr.00@list.ru>
Signed-off-by: immanuwell <pchpr.00@list.ru>

fix(authn): fix JSON struct tag typo in kubernetes auth claims (#5908)

The Expiration field in the claims struct had a typo in its struct tag:

jsom:"exp" → json:"exp"

This caused Go's encoding/json to never unmarshal the exp field from
the Kubernetes service account JWT, leaving Expiration always as 0
(Unix epoch). Downstream this causes token expiry to be treated as
January 1, 1970, effectively making all SA tokens immediately expired

fix(ofrep): new SSE event stream endpoint and conditional request support (#5957)

- The origin field was marked as optional in grpc and it was always returned as an empty string, which breaks the ofrep-web JS client logic for constructing the streaming URL.
- The snapshotDigest was removed to align with current implementation details in the ofrep-web JS client. Removing it causes an extra re-evaluation fetch to the bulk endpoint on each (re)connect. Ideally, it should be avoided but I don't see a good solution at the moment.
- Include Etag in CORS exposed headers for cross-origin reads. The Access-Control-Expose-Headers response header only listed Link, preventing browser JS from reading the Etag header cross-origin. This broke conditional request caching via If-None-Match. Added Etag to the exposed headers list.
- Move SSE stream endpoint to /ofrep/v1/_stream/{env}/{ns}/events to support skip authentication for in-process OFREP stream requests

related #5669 61aa322bc

Fix CUE validation for boolean rollouts and null descriptions (#5385)

* Fix CUE validation for boolean rollouts and null descriptions

* test: add validation tests for null descriptions and boolean flag types

Added comprehensive tests to catch the bugs fixed in the CUE schema validation:

1. TestValidate_NullDescriptions: Verifies that null values are accepted
   for description fields in namespaces, flags, variants, segments,
   constraints, and rollouts. This would have caught the bug where the
   schema was incorrectly rejecting null descriptions.

2. TestValidate_VariantFlagWithoutRollouts: Validates that variant flags
   do not require the rollouts field. This would have caught the bug where
   the unconditional #FlagBoolean | *{} pattern was incorrectly requiring
   rollouts on all flag types.

Also updated existing test fixtures to explicitly declare type: BOOLEAN_FLAG_TYPE
for boolean flags, as the schema now properly enforces that only boolean flags
can have rollouts.

orphaned — not an ancestor of v2. goreleaser determines the changelog's
previous tag via `git describe --tags --abbrev=0 <tag>^`, which skips
orphaned tags and walks back to the last reachable one. For v2.10.0 this
fell all the way back to v2.7.0, so the release notes spanned three
releases (252 commits instead of 88).

Compute the previous release tag by semver order and pass it to
goreleaser via GORELEASER_PREVIOUS_TAG, so the changelog stays scoped to
a single release regardless of tag ancestry. Empty for the first release,
in which case goreleaser falls back to its default behavior.

docs(release): tag the squashed merge commit and verify reachability (#6083)

The release process squash-merges the release PR into v2, which produces a
new commit SHA on the branch. The annotated tag must point at that squashed
commit on origin/v2, not at the local release-branch commit — otherwise the
tag is orphaned (not an ancestor of v2) and goreleaser's changelog for the
next release walks back past it to a much older tag. This is what produced
the v2.10.0 release notes spanning three releases.

Tighten steps 6-7 of the release command:
- Hard-sync local v2 to origin/v2 and confirm HEAD is the squashed release
  commit before tagging.
- Add a reachability gate: verify `git merge-base --is-ancestor` before
  pushing the tag, and abort if it fails.

root cause rather than just tolerating it.

fix(server): downgrade 'authentication required' gRPC log to WARN (#6198)

Unauthenticated requests to the login flow are expected behavior, not
an error condition. Logging them at ERROR produced a false-positive
ERROR line on every UI login, tripping monitoring and alerting.

Downgrade only the two 'authentication required' interceptor lines
(unary + stream) from Error to Warn. Genuine auth failures (metadata
missing, email not allowed, email-matching errors) continue to log at
ERROR.

Fixes #6186

fix(validation): correct less-than operator from "le" to "lt" in schema (#6304)

The CUE schema (and the JSON Schema mirror) listed the less-than
operator for NUMBER_COMPARISON_TYPE and DATETIME_COMPARISON_TYPE
constraints as "le" instead of "lt". The rest of the codebase
(rpc/flipt/operators.go OpLT, the evaluator, and its tests) uses
"lt", so any segment with a less-than constraint failed schema
validation with a confusing empty-disjunction error, e.g.:

    segments.0.constraints.0: 4 errors in empty disjunction:
    segments.0.constraints.0.type: conflicting values
    "STRING_COMPARISON_TYPE" and "NUMBER_COMPARISON_TYPE" ...

Note the asymmetry prior to this change: the schema allowed gt and
gte on the greater-than side, but le and lte on the less-than side.

- Replace "le" with "lt" in flipt.cue for number and datetime
  constraint operators
- Same fix in the flipt.json JSON Schema
- Add TestValidate_ConstraintLTOperator covering lt constraints for
  both number and datetime types (fails before this fix, passes after)

Signed-off-by: Islam Diab <iislamddiab2001@gmail.com>

feat(authn/jwt): expose full claims as io.flipt.auth.claims metadata (#6361)

* feat(authn/jwt): expose full claims as io.flipt.auth.claims metadata

The JWT authentication method only promotes a fixed set of user attributes
into authentication metadata. `claims_mapping` cannot be used to reach the
others, since its keys are validated against a closed allowlist (email, sub,
picture, name, role). Authorization policies therefore have no way to
reference non-standard root-level claims such as `client_id` or `scope`,
which is how machine-to-machine tokens carry their identity.

Marshal the full claim set into `io.flipt.auth.claims`, matching the OIDC
method, which already populates the same key. Rego policies can then
`json.unmarshal` it to reach any claim the token carries.

The key is written after the mapped attributes so that it always wins over
an `io.flipt.auth.claims` claim carried within the token itself, and a
marshalling failure fails authentication closed rather than proceeding with
metadata the policy engine would evaluate against.

chore(deps): bump tooling and Go module dependencies (#6507)

Bump developer tool versions in .mise.toml (go 1.27, golangci-lint
2.13.2, buf 1.72.0, mockery 3.8.0) and update golang.org/x/* module
dependencies to their latest patch releases.

Also permit unused core import required for openapi generation.
environments.proto imports core/core.proto so protoc-gen-
flipt-openapi receives the Flag/Segment descriptors it injects into
the management API OpenAPI document. The types are not referenced by
the proto itself, so buf 1.72.0 complains that the import as unused
(IMPORT_USED). Scope an ignore_only exception for this file rather
than removing the import, which would break the generated openapi.yaml.

Signed-off-by: Roman Dmytrenko <rdmytrenko@gmail.com>
fix(storage/git): use git-safe environment names for branch refs (#6508)

fix(build): repair the go:modernize task (#6509)

The task ran the standalone modernize tool at @latest with
-category=-omitzero. gopls v0.23.0 turned modernize into a multi-analyzer
checker with one boolean flag per analysis and removed -category, so the
task now fails before it examines any code:

    flag provided but not defined: -category

CI is unaffected because it runs golangci-lint, which enables the
modernize linter and disables the omitzero and stringsbuilder analyses
in .golangci.yml. The local task and CI had drifted apart.

Run modernize through golangci-lint instead. The set of enabled analyses
now lives only in .golangci.yml, so the task matches CI and cannot break
again when the upstream tool changes its flags.

Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01W2Q8KrTDLTeKQ5zKRxDwAg

fix(evaluation): return FLAG_DISABLED for disabled boolean flag with no rollouts (#6515)

Boolean evaluation previously fell through to the default path, returning DEFAULT_EVALUATION_REASON
for a disabled flag with no rollouts. This was inconsistent with the variant path, which returns
 FLAG_DISABLED_EVALUATION_REASON. Add an early return in boolean() when and there are no rollouts.

Some OIDC providers use non-standard claims for user information,
which can leave Flipt sessions without the expected email, name,
picture, or sub claims. Add claims_mapping to allow these claims
to be mapped to Flipt's expected session fields.

fix(license): enforce expiry consistently and harden offline license validation (#6539)

* test(license): cover offline bridge license files

Signed-off-by: Mark Phelps <209477+markphelps@users.noreply.github.com>

* fix(license): honor expiry on cached license validation

The cached branch of validateAndSet set product.Pro without checking the
license expiry. Since validations are cached for 6h, a license expiring
inside that window kept Pro features enabled until the cache entry aged
out.

Consolidate the expiry check into a hasValidExpiry helper and use it in
all three places that need it: the cached path, the post-validation
check, and Product().

Also drop the setOSSProduct helper and set the product inline at each
call site so no method acquires lm.mu on a caller's behalf, removing the
risk of acquiring the same lock twice.

Signed-off-by: Mark Phelps <209477+markphelps@users.noreply.github.com>

* The rate-limit branch of validateAndSet kept Pro features whenever a
prior license object existed, even if it was expired or had no expiry.
Check hasValidExpiry instead so only an unexpired license survives a
rate-limit error; otherwise fall back to OSS.

fix(ui): match Combobox options by display name, not only key (#6550)

* fix(ui): match Combobox options by display name, not only key

Combobox renders each option as a CommandItem with value={item.key}, and
cmdk's default filter scores the search term against that value. The
display name was never part of the searchable text, so typing a segment
name returned no results on the flag rollout form.

command-score normalises "-" and whitespace the same way, which is why
this only shows up when the key differs from the name: "Test Rollout"
still matches the key "test-rollout", but "Beta Cohort" scores 0 against
the key "seg-1234".

cmdk's CommandItem accepts a keywords prop that the default filter folds
into the scored text, so passing the display name there makes both the
key and the name searchable. Verified against cmdk 1.1.1 defaultFilter:
("seg-1234", "Beta") scores 0, ("seg-1234", "Beta", ["Beta Cohort"])
scores 0.891.

This fixes the reported segment picker and also applies to the other
Combobox users: the flag picker on distributions, analytics and console.

Fixes #6549
